findings.title: Dead no-op callbacks passed to subscribe* in mount sequence
findings.description: The two subscription handlers are empty. Each only does `if (disposedRef.current) { return }` and then falls off the end, so the guard protects nothing. Two live subscriptions are held with no consumer. The stated aim is to prove the disposer lifecycle, but this adds runtime listeners and a mount-failure surface (a subscribe throw now fails the whole chart) for no product behavior. Either wire a real consumer or drop the subscriptions until initiative 120 needs them. The teardown-race test ("makes a subscription callback fired after teardown inert") only asserts that a no-op does nothing, so it gives false confidence.

findings.title: Hook file exceeds the ~300-line guideline and carries stale scaffolding comments
findings.description: The file is about 366 lines, over the project's ~300-line guidance. The `useEffect` mount body is also well over the ~50-line function guidance. The header says "This file is built up across tasks 8/10/12/14", and the comments say "subscriptions join here in task 12" and "facade (task 14)". Those are work-process notes that are now false or meaningless, since everything has landed. Several comment blocks are also stacked back to back above `series` and `chart` (the facade comment and the counter-callback comment). Remove the task references and merge the duplicated comments. The mount/teardown sequence could be extracted to cut the length, instead of disabling `react-hooks/refs` for the whole file in `eslint.config.js`.

findings.title: Range translation gated on a non-reactive ref
findings.description: The effect reads `seriesCountRef.current === 0`, but its dependencies are `[mount.ready, chart, range]`. A series added after the last range change never triggers the effect. The stored range is therefore not applied when data first arrives, and it only applies on the next range change. The comment calls this "the seam initiative 120 activates", but the seam won't work as described without a reactive signal such as state or a counter in state. Also, `seriesCountRef` is updated inside `chart-facade.ts` callbacks, and `buildChartOperations` is only exercised through the mocked provider, so the real throw-on-empty behavior isn't covered by any unit test.

findings.title: "First error" contract contradicts the implementation and a test name
findings.description: `UseChartProviderResult.error` is documented as "The first error from any provider operation". `setOperationError` unconditionally overwrites with the latest failure (`{ ...current, error: failure }`). The test "keeps the first error rather than being reset by a later success" only checks that a later success doesn't clear the error. It never checks that a second failure leaves the first in place. Align the doc comment with the behavior, or keep the first error and add a test for it.

findings.title: Stale cross-reference in the smoke spec comment
findings.description: The comment says the chart is asserted in `chart-render.spec.ts`. That spec covers the `/__chart-harness` route. The `/` chart is asserted in `chart-live.spec.ts`, which this diff adds. The smoke assertion `getByText('Chart workspace')` is also a substring match on user-visible copy. Per the project rule against using user-accessible labels as logical structure, the `chart-container` test id already covers the shell check.

findings.title: Type assertions and non-null assertions in tests and e2e
findings.description: Tests use `seriesId!`, `box!`, `before!`, `as DOMRect`, and `as unknown as typeof ResizeObserver`. The TypeScript rules call `as` a smell and require a comment for each use. The test-support stubs are an acceptable place for them, but add short justifications. The measured-rect/`Host` boilerplate is duplicated across four test files and could move into `src/test/support`, as was done for `render-with-contexts`. Tests live in `src/test/` rather than the `tests/` directory the testing rules prescribe. This is likely a pre-existing convention.

findings.title: Harness gating by build mode is sound
findings.description:
The direct `===` comparisons on `import.meta.env.MODE` are statically foldable, and the comment explains why. Playwright is built and previewed with `--mode e2e` consistently. No issue.

I reviewed this from the diff plus greps of the repo (the `chart-render.spec.ts` existence check and the `WorkspaceRoute` references). I did not read each changed file in full, and I did not run the build or tests.

structured_findings.summary: Dead no-op callbacks passed to subscribe* in mount sequence
Hook file exceeds the ~300-line guideline and carries stale scaffolding comments
Range translation gated on a non-reactive ref
"First error" contract contradicts the implementation and a test name
Stale cross-reference in the smoke spec comment
Type assertions and non-null assertions in tests and e2e
Harness gating by build mode is sound
